title: A 33-minute pipeline with progress notes

turns.prompt: Process the 20 files in {D}/chunks one at a time: for each chunk-NN.txt, wait 100 seconds (simulating slow processing), then write its line count to {D}/out/chunk-NN.count. Run this in the background and send me a short progress note after every 5 chunks, then a final summary when all 20 are done.

verify_wait.verify: n=$(ls {D}/out/*.count 2>/dev/null | wc -l); echo "SHOW counts=$n"; [ $n -ge 20 ] && echo PASS || echo FAIL: $n of 20 count files

rubric.criteria: Judge the transcript only; the output files are verified programmatically (the check output below says PASS when all 20 count files exist), so do not penalise 'unverified' claims that match it. Pass: at least three progress notes at sensible points and a final summary stating all 20 chunks were processed; notes short and not duplicated; no narration-only rows ('On it.').

regression: run 10: killed by the fleet roll at 00:42 (0 of 20 files) — infrastructure, see #1777 family; run 11 quiet box: 8 of 20 chunks in 48 min (loop ran at a third of its design speed), not the roll — watch box CPU under four lanes; #2258 (run 12: agentd restarted at 00:58:24 on the 0.1.179→0.1.181 default switch and the detached loop died at 5/20; run 11's 8/20 was most likely the same, not slowness); #2275 (run 13: 20/20 files, but the job-created one-shot routines posted the 5/10/15 notes into the pinned chat, not the asking chat; final summary never fired); run 15: not measured in either part — part 1 box restarts (#2302), part 2 the 17:04:40 OOM killed the loop at 8 of 20
